Both the Unitree G1 and the Booster K1 are compact, highly capable humanoid robots targeted at research, development, and education, but they differ significantly in size, design focus, price point, and performance specs.

Key Specifications Comparison

Feature
Unitree G1 (Base / EDU)
Booster K1 (Geek / Edu / Pro)
Height
~130 cm (1.3 m)
~95 cm
Weight
~35 kg
~19.5 kg
Degrees of Freedom (DoF)
23 DoF base (scales up to 29–43+ DoF on EDU versions with dexterous hands)
22 DoF (Legs: 6x2, Arms: 4x2, Head: 2)
Sensors
Livox Mid-360 3D LiDAR, Intel RealSense D435i depth camera, mic array
Stereo/depth camera, 9-axis IMU, microphone array, speaker
Onboard Computing
High-performance CPU (Base) / NVIDIA Jetson Orin up to 100–157 TOPS (EDU)
Configurable AI compute ranging from 48 up to 200 TOPS
Battery Life
Roughly 2 hours under active use
~50 minutes to 1 hour 20 minutes (depending on model and load)
Price Range
Starts around $14,000 to over $40,000+ for advanced EDU variants
Generally spans roughly $5,999 (Geek entry version) up to higher-tier configurations

Core Differences

1. Size and Form Factor

Unitree G1: Taller and heavier (~1.3m, 35 kg), giving it a more human-like proportion. It features advanced joint torque capabilities and can handle dynamic movements like jumping, spinning, and agile locomotion.

Booster K1: Shorter and much lighter (~95 cm, 19.5 kg). Its compact, portable footprint makes it exceptionally easy to move between classrooms and tight laboratory spaces without requiring rigorous safety rigging.

2. Target Use Cases & Openness

Unitree G1: Well-known for high agility and dynamic movement (running, deep reinforcement learning, and complex manipulation). However, keep in mind that entry-level or base G1 versions can sometimes come with software locks, meaning full secondary development capabilities often require stepping up to higher-priced EDU packages.

Booster K1: Positioned heavily as an accessible developer and STEM education platform. Even entry configurations (like the K1 Geek) offer open-source tools and secondary development support out of the box for Python, ROS, and ROS2, making it popular for university labs on a tighter budget.

3. Hardware & Sensors

Unitree G1: Equipped out-of-the-box with heavy-duty sensing like a 3D LiDAR (Livox Mid-360), making it robust for complex indoor mapping and autonomous navigation.

Booster K1: Relies primarily on vision-based depth/stereo cameras and an IMU for its perception stack, trading away heavy LiDAR sensors to maintain a lighter weight and lower price tag.

Which one should you choose?

Go with the Unitree G1 if: You need a larger, faster, highly dynamic platform capable of advanced research into bipedal locomotion, heavy manipulation, and complex AI simulation where LiDAR mapping and higher physical payloads are required.

Go with the Booster K1 if: You are looking for a more affordable, highly portable, classroom-friendly desktop-to-floor humanoid robot focused on Python/ROS2 programming, basic machine learning, and human-robot interaction without spending enterprise-level budgets.
